memory_update.text: VPG should be tracked as an underfollowed US-listed precision force/strain sensor candidate for robotics; key survival test is whether humanoid orders become material production revenue rather than prototype activity.

ALNT should be tracked as an underfollowed US-listed motion-control and actuation subsystem candidate; key survival test is proof of qualified robotics sockets, especially motors, drives, gearheads, encoders, or integrated actuator modules.
CGNX is a machine-vision reference anchor, not the primary alpha-hunt target; use it to benchmark automation/vision demand and market attention against smaller suppliers.

Rare-earth magnet exposure was not fully expanded in this at-most-3-candidate pass. MP Materials has direct rare-earth and magnet-manufacturing relevance and should be considered in a separate materials/magnets sub-pass, but it is higher-attention than VPG and ALNT.
Harmonic reducer pure-play exposure remains limited in US listings; likely public candidates are more available in Japan, China, Taiwan, and Korea, requiring a non-US or ADR-focused pass.

summary: Expanded a focused US-listed universe for the robotics precision-motion and sensing node. This pass prioritizes underfollowed component and sensor suppliers rather than humanoid robot assemblers. The strongest underfollowed candidates found are VPG for precision force/strain sensing and ALNT for controlled motion, motors, drives, gearing, encoders, and actuation subsystems. CGNX is included as a reference/context anchor for machine vision because it is less obscure but maps directly to industrial vision and factory automation. No buy/sell view is implied.
